SAS INPUT(source, <? | ??> informat.)

Source: R/doc_functions.R
sas_f_input.Rd

Reads a value with an informat. See the SAS documentation (Functions and CALL Routines).

Arguments

s

Source value to read; a numeric source is first converted with BEST12.

fmt

Parsed informat specification: a list with elements name, w, d, char and text, as produced by the translator from a informat written as name w.d (e.g. 8.3, z5., $5.). In SAS code this is the informat name itself, not a string.

qq

Error-control modifier written before the informat: ” (default) writes a note and sets the error flag for invalid data; '?' suppresses the note; '??' suppresses the note and the error flag.

.at

Internal: source position c(line, column) used in log NOTEs.

Value

A vector with one result per element (arguments are recycled), as the SAS function returns per observation.

Differences from R

Implements the SAS DATA step semantics (log NOTEs, _ERROR_), which base R has no counterpart for.

See also

Other special functions: sas_f_band(), sas_f_blshift(), sas_f_bnot(), sas_f_bor(), sas_f_brshift(), sas_f_bxor(), sas_f_exist(), sas_f_inputc(), sas_f_inputn(), sas_f_missing(), sas_f_nvalid(), sas_f_prxchange(), sas_f_prxmatch(), sas_f_prxparse(), sas_f_put(), sas_f_putc(), sas_f_putn()

Examples

# INPUT: each call is explained above it and followed by its result

# INPUT reads the character value '123' with the numeric informat 8. and
# returns the number 123.
sas_f_input("123", list(name = "", w = 8L, d = NA_integer_, char = FALSE, text = "8."))  # input('123', 8.) = 123
#> [1] 123

# With informat 4.2 and no decimal point in the data, the last 2 digits are
# taken as decimals: 12.34.
sas_f_input("1234", list(name = "", w = 4L, d = 2L, char = FALSE, text = "4.2"))  # input('1234', 4.2) = 12.34
#> [1] 12.34

# The COMMA informat removes the commas before reading the number.
sas_f_input("1,234", list(name = "comma", w = 8L, d = NA_integer_, char = FALSE, text = "comma8."))  # input('1,234', comma8.) = 1234
#> [1] 1234

# The ?? modifier suppresses the invalid-data note and the error flag; the
# unreadable value gives missing.
sas_f_input("abc", list(name = "", w = 8L, d = NA_integer_, char = FALSE, text = "8."), qq = "??")  # input('abc', ?? 8.) = .
#> [1] NA

# The character informat $3. reads only the first 3 characters.
sas_f_input("abcdef", list(name = "", w = 3L, d = NA_integer_, char = TRUE, text = "$3."))  # input('abcdef', $3.) = "abc"
#> [1] "abc"
